Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 1:

﴿Alif, Lam, Ra﴾ I am Allah, the All-Seeing. ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾ These are the verses that I have sent down to you, the verses of the Qur'an. ﴿The Wise﴾ the one who judges between people.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 2:

﴿Was it a wonder for the people﴾ (i.e., the people of Makkah) ﴿that We revealed to a man from among them﴾? And this is because they said: "Did God not find anyone to send to us except the orphan of Abu Talib?" ﴿to warn the people and give good tidings to those who believe﴾, meaning: We sent him as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner. ﴿that they will have a sure standing with their Lord﴾, meaning: the righteous deeds. ﴿The disbelievers said: "Indeed, this [Qur'an] is clear magic."﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 3:

﴿Indeed, your Lord is Allah﴾, explained in Surat al-A'raf. And His saying ﴿who arranges the affair﴾ means He decrees it. ﴿There is no intercessor except after His permission﴾ is a refutation of their saying: "The idols are our intercessors with Allah."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 5:

﴿He it is who made the sun a radiance﴾, meaning possessing radiance, ﴿and the moon a light﴾, meaning possessing light, ﴿and determined for it stages﴾, meaning He determined for it stages according to the number of the days of the month. ﴿God did not create that﴾, meaning what has been mentioned, ﴿except in truth﴾, meaning with justice; that is, He is just in His creation, and He did not create it in injustice or in vanity. ﴿He details the signs﴾, meaning He makes them clear, ﴿for a people who know﴾, meaning who draw inference from them about the power of God.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 7:

﴿Indeed, those who do not expect to meet Us﴾ — they do not fear the resurrection (al-ba'th). ﴿And they are content with the worldly life﴾ instead of the Hereafter. ﴿And they are at rest therein﴾ and inclined to it. ﴿And those who are heedless of Our signs﴾ — what I have sent down of the lawful and the unlawful and the legal prescriptions (al-shara'i') — ﴿are heedless.﴾

Translation:

"And His words: ﴿Their Lord guides them by their faith﴾ meaning: to the Gardens, as a reward for them for their faith."

Their call therein will be: "Glory be to You, O Allah" (﴿Glory be to You, O Allah﴾). That is, whenever they desire something, they say, "Glory be to You, O Allah," and what they desire comes to them. Then, when they have eaten of what they desire, they say, "Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds" (﴿All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 11:

﴿And if Allah were to hasten for people the evil⦆ — the verse was revealed concerning a man's supplication against himself, his family and his children with what he dislikes, that it be answered for him. The meaning: "If I were to answer them in evil as they love to be answered in good," ﴿then their term would have been decreed for them﴾ — they would have died and their destruction would have been completed. It was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith when he said: ﴿O Allah, if this is indeed the truth from You⦆ — the verse. This is indicated by His saying: ﴿So We leave those who do not expect meeting Us﴾, meaning: the disbelievers who do not fear resurrection.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 12:

﴿And when harm touches man﴾, meaning: the disbeliever, ﴿harm﴾, meaning sickness and affliction, ﴿he calls upon Us, lying on his side﴾, meaning: lying down, ﴿or sitting or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he passes on﴾, meaning: he persists in arrogance, refusing to give thanks, ﴿as if he had never called upon Us for a harm that touched him﴾, due to his forgetting what he called upon God for in it and what God did for him. ﴿Thus has it been made attractive﴾, just as the calling upon God in affliction and the turning away in ease was made attractive to this disbeliever, ﴿made attractive to the transgressors﴾ their deeds, namely those who transgressed against themselves when they worshipped the idol.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 13:

﴿And We did destroy generations before you﴾ He warns the disbelievers of Makkah with the like of the punishment of the earlier nations. ﴿And they were not going to believe﴾ because Allah sealed their hearts as a recompense for them for their disbelief. ﴿Thus do We recompense the criminal people﴾ We will do to those who denied Muhammad (ﷺ) as We did to those before them, as a recompense for their disbelief.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 14:

﴿Then We made you successors in the land after them﴾ meaning: the people of Makkah. ﴿That We might observe how you would act﴾ that We might test your deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 15:

﴿And when Our verses are recited to them, clear as they are,﴾ to these polytheists, ﴿those who do not expect to meet Us say:﴾ that is, those who do not fear the Resurrection (al-ba'th), ﴿"Bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it."﴾ That is, one that contains no criticism of our gods. ﴿Or change it⦆ — speak it from your own self, and then alter in it what we dislike.

﴿Say: "It is not for me to change it on my own accord."﴾ That is, it is not fitting for me to alter it from my own self. ﴿"I follow only what is revealed to me."﴾ That is, I tell you only what God has informed me of; meaning, what I have brought is from God, not from my own self, so that I would change it.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 16:

﴿Say: "If Allah had willed, I would not have recited it to you, nor would He have made you know of it."﴾ I did not recite the Qur'an to you. ﴿Nor would He have made you know of it.﴾ Nor would Allah have informed you of it. ﴿For I had already lived among you a lifetime before it.﴾ I remained among you forty years, not telling you anything. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ That it is not from me.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 17:

﴿Who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah?﴾ No one is more unjust than one who wrongs with the wrong of disbelief. That is: I have not fabricated against Allah nor lied about Him, but you have done that, when you claimed that He has a partner. ﴿Indeed, the criminals will not succeed.﴾ Whoever denies the prophets of Allah will not attain happiness.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 18:

﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which can neither harm them﴾ if they do not worship Him, ﴿nor benefit them﴾ if they do worship Him. ﴿And they say, "These are our intercessors with Allah."﴾ concerning the setting right of their livelihood in this world, because they do not affirm the Resurrection. ﴿Say, "Do you inform Allah of what He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?"﴾ Do you tell Allah that He has a partner, when Allah, glorified is He, does not know of any partner for Himself in the heavens or on the earth? Then He declared Himself far above what they invent, so He said: ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He above what they associate.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 19:

﴿And mankind was not but one community﴾ meaning: from the time of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) until ʿAmr ibn Luhayy changed the religion, ﴿then they differed﴾ and took up idols, ﴿and had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾ [i.e., the delay of the punishment of this community until the Day of Resurrection], ﴿the matter would have been decided between them﴾ [i.e., by the descent of the punishment].

And they say, [meaning the people of Makkah]: "Why not" (lula, i.e. "why has it not been sent down"), "a sign from his Lord?" [such as the staff and what the prophets brought]. Say: "The unseen belongs only to Allah." That is: your saying, "Why has a sign not been sent down to him?" is a matter of the unseen, and the unseen belongs only to Allah; no one knows why He has not done that. ﴿So wait﴾ for the sign to be sent down. ﴿Indeed, I am with you among those who wait.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 21:

﴿And when We let the people﴾ (i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah) ﴿taste mercy﴾ (i.e., rain and fertility) ﴿after adversity had touched them﴾ (i.e., poverty and hardship), ﴿behold, they have a scheme against Our signs.﴾ (i.e., a statement of denial). That is: when they are blessed with abundance, they become arrogant and devise ways to repel the signs of God. ﴿Say: God is swifter in scheming.﴾ (i.e., swifter in retribution). That is: the punishment that comes to them is swifter in destroying them than the scheming they undertook to nullify the signs of God. ﴿Indeed Our messengers﴾ (i.e., the guardian angels) ﴿record what you scheme,﴾ in order to requite you for it in the Hereafter.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 22:

﴿He is the One who enables you to travel on land﴾ on mounts and beasts, ﴿and on sea﴾ on ships. ﴿Until, when you are in the ship﴾ the ships, ﴿and they sail with them﴾ meaning: the ships sailed with those who boarded them at sea, ﴿with a fair wind﴾ a gentle, mild breeze, ﴿and they rejoice﴾ at that wind, because of its gentleness and steadiness. ﴿There comes to it a violent wind﴾ a severe one, ﴿and the waves come to them﴾ and it is what rises of the water, ﴿from every place﴾ in the sea, ﴿and they think that they are encompassed﴾ they have drawn near to destruction. ﴿They call upon Allah, sincere to Him in religion﴾ they abandoned polytheism and sincerely devoted lordship to Allah, and they said: ﴿If You save us from this﴾ violent wind, ﴿we will surely be among the grateful﴾ the monotheists, the obedient.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 23:

﴿So when He saved them, behold, they committed outrage on earth without right.﴾ They were acting with corruption, sins, and audacity against Allah. ﴿O mankind, your outrage is only against yourselves.﴾ That is: "Some of you transgressing against others." ﴿It is but the enjoyment of worldly life.﴾ That is: what they attain through this corruption and transgression, they only enjoy in the life of this world. ﴿Then to Us is your return.﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 24:

﴿Indeed, the likeness of the worldly life﴾ means: the perishable life in this abode, ﴿is like water﴾, like rain, ﴿which We sent down from the sky, and the vegetation of the earth mingled with it﴾ by that rain and because of it ﴿grows, of which men eat﴾ such as herbs, grains and fruits, ﴿and cattle﴾ from pasture and fodder. ﴿Until, when the earth has taken on its adornment﴾ its ornament and beauty, ﴿and is decked out﴾ with its plants, ﴿and its people think they have power over it﴾ to harvest it and benefit from it, ﴿Our command comes to it﴾ Our punishment, ﴿and We make it a harvested field﴾ with nothing left in it, ﴿as if it had not flourished﴾ as if it had not been there yesterday. ﴿Thus﴾ is the life of this world: it is a means of gathering wealth, and the splendour of this world, until that wealth becomes abundant in the hands of its owner and he thinks he will enjoy it, and then it is taken from him by death or by an event that destroys it. ﴿Thus We detail the signs﴾ just as We have explained this parable of the worldly life, so Allah explains the verses of the Qur'an ﴿for a people who reflect﴾ upon the Return (al-ma'ad).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 25:

﴿And Allah invites to the Abode of Peace﴾, which is Paradise, through the sending of the Messenger and the setting up of proofs; ﴿and guides whom He wills﴾. He made the invitation general and restricted guidance to whomever He wills.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 26:

﴿For those who did good﴾ — they said: "There is no god but Allah." ﴿Is the best reward﴾ — Paradise. ﴿And more﴾ — gazing upon the Noble Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And neither dust nor humiliation will cover their faces﴾ — i.e., will overcast them: ﴿dust﴾ means blackness from sorrow. ﴿Nor humiliation﴾ as befalls the people of Hell. And this is after their gazing upon their Lord, Blessed and Exalted.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 27:

﴿And those who earned evil deeds﴾ — they practiced shirk (associating partners with God) — ﴿the recompense of an evil deed is its like﴾, meaning: for them is the recompense of an evil deed, ﴿like it﴾, ﴿and humiliation will cover them﴾ — there will befall them abasement, disgrace and degradation — ﴿they will have from God no protector﴾ — from the punishment of God, no one to preserve them ﴿from any defender﴾, no one who will prevent them. ﴿As if their faces had been covered﴾ — were clothed — ﴿with pieces of the night﴾ — a portion of it — ﴿dark﴾.

﴿And on the Day We gather them all﴾: We gather them all, the disbelievers and their deities. ﴿Then We will say to those who associated others with Allah: "Stay in your place"﴾: halt and remain in your place. ﴿You and your partners. Then We will separate them﴾: We divide and distinguish them, [namely] the polytheists from their partners, and the connection that existed between them in the world is severed. ﴿And their partners will say﴾, and they are the idols: ﴿"You did not worship us"﴾. They deny their worship and say: "We were not aware that you were worshipping us." And Allah makes them speak this.

Verse 29 of the surah has a shortened form: ﴿Then God is sufficient as a witness between us﴾ and so on. This is the speech of the associators (al-shuraka'). They said: God bears witness, in His knowledge, concerning us that ﴿we were not aware of your worship﴾ except as unaware, because we were inanimate objects (jamad) in which there was no spirit (ruh).

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 30:

﴿Hunalika﴾ (there), at that time, ﴿every soul will be tested by what it sent before﴾, meaning it will receive the recompense for what it had already done, of good or evil. ﴿And they will be returned to God, their true Master﴾, meaning: the One who holds authority over their affairs and will requite them with truth. ﴿And what they used to fabricate will vanish from them﴾, meaning it will depart and be nullified, ﴿what they used to fabricate﴾ in the world of lies and denial.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 31:

﴿Say: Who provides for you from the heaven and the earth?﴾ Who sends down rain from the sky and brings forth vegetation from the earth?

﴿Or who controls hearing and sight?﴾ Who made them and created them for you? In the sense of: who controls their creation.

﴿And who brings the living out of the dead?﴾ The believer from the disbeliever, and vegetation from the earth, and the human from the drop of semen, and the reverse of that.

﴿And who brings the dead out of the living and who arranges﴾ the affair of this world and the Hereafter.

﴿They will say, "Allah."﴾ That is: Allah, the One who does these things. So when they acknowledge this after the argument against them,

﴿So say: Will you not then be wary?﴾ Will you not fear Allah, so that you do not associate anything with Him?

So that is Allah, your true Lord. That is, the One to whom all this belongs as His act is the Truth; not these whom you have made partners with Him. ﴿So what is there after the truth but error?﴾ After worshipping Allah, ﴿but error﴾ means: the worship of Satan. ﴿How, then, are you turned away?﴾ He means: how are your minds turned away to worshipping one who provides no sustenance, gives no life, and causes no death?

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 33:

﴿Thus﴾ (i.e., so) ﴿has the word of your Lord been justified﴾ (i.e., proven true) ﴿concerning those who defied﴾ (i.e., persisted rebelliously in disbelief) ﴿that they will not believe﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 35:

﴿Say: "Is there any of your associates who guides to the truth?"﴾ That is, your gods. ﴿Who guides﴾ means who directs ﴿to the truth﴾, to the religion of Islam. ﴿Say: "It is Allah who guides to the truth."﴾ That is, to the truth. ﴿Is one who guides to the truth more worthy to be followed, or one who does not guide unless he is guided?﴾ That is: Allah, who guides and directs the people of truth to the truth, is more worthy that His command be followed, or the idols that guide no one? ﴿Unless he is guided﴾ means directed. They themselves, even if they were guided, would not be guided; but the speech was revealed in the manner that if they were guided they would be guided, because when they took them as gods, He spoke of them as one speaks of those who have knowledge. ﴿What is wrong with you?﴾ That is, what is there for you in worshipping idols? This is a complete statement. ﴿How do you judge?﴾ That is, how do you decide, when you claim that there is a partner with Allah?

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 36:

﴿And most of them follow not except assumption.﴾ He means: the leaders, because the common people follow their statements. ﴿Indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all.﴾ Assumption is not like certainty; i.e., assumption does not take the place of knowledge. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾ Of their disbelief.

This is a Qur'anic verse quotation with an explanation. Translate faithfully.

Verse-quote translation: "And it was not [possible] that this Qur'an be fabricated apart from Allah..."

"Ta'wil"? Not needed. Technical terms: none needing gloss except maybe none. Keep ﴿ ﴾ markers.

"ائت بقرآن غير هذا" = "Bring a Qur'an other than this."

in English.

**Translation:**

﴿And it was not [possible] that this Qur'an be fabricated apart from Allah﴾. This is an answer to their saying: ﴿Bring a Qur'an other than this﴾. He says: this Qur'an is not a fabrication apart from Allah. ﴿But it is a confirmation﴾, but it is a confirmation of ﴿what is before it﴾ of the scriptures, ﴿and a detailed explanation of the Book﴾, meaning: a detailed explanation of what has been written of the promise for whoever believes and the threat for whoever disobeys, ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾, there is no doubt that it has been sent down from the Lord of the worlds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 38:

﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾ Rather, do you say, "Muhammad has fabricated it"? ﴿Say: Then bring a surah like it﴾ if it is fabricated, ﴿and call upon﴾ for help in matching it ﴿whomever you are able to, besides Allah, if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that Muhammad invented it of his own accord. The parallel to this verse is in Surat al-Baqarah: ﴿And if you are in doubt﴾ ... the verse.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 39:

﴿Nay, they denied what they had not encompassed in knowledge﴾, meaning: what the Qur'an contains of Paradise, the Fire, the resurrection and the Final Hour. ﴿And its interpretation had not yet come to them﴾, meaning: the reality of what they were promised in the Book had not yet come to them. ﴿Thus did those before them deny﴾ the resurrection and the Final Hour.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 40:

﴿And among them﴾ — that is, among the disbelievers of Makkah — ﴿are those who believe in it﴾, meaning: a people whom He knew would believe. ﴿And among them are those who do not believe in it. And your Lord is most knowing of the corrupters.﴾ He means: the deniers. And this is a threat to them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 41:

﴿And if they deny you, say: "For me is my deed"﴾ The verse was abrogated (naskh) by the verse of jihad.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 42:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you.﴾ It was revealed concerning the mockers, who would listen to the mockery and the denial. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Can you make the deaf hear?﴾ He means that they are like the deaf, because of the intensity of their enmity. ﴿And even if they lacked understanding.﴾ That is: and even if they were, along with being deaf, ignorant! Allah the Glorified informed that they are like deaf and ignorant people, since they did not benefit from what they heard.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 43:

﴿And among them are those who look at you﴾ in astonishment at you, gaining nothing from their looking. ﴿Would you then guide the blind, even though they do not see?﴾ He means: God has blinded their hearts, so they do not perceive anything of guidance.

Indeed, Allah does not wrong the people in anything. When He mentioned the people of wretchedness (ash-shaqawa), He mentioned that He did not wrong them by decreeing wretchedness upon them, because He disposes of His own dominion. ﴿But it is the people themselves who wrong themselves.﴾ through their earning of sins.

﴿And the day He gathers them, [it will seem] as though they had not remained [in the world] except an hour of the day.﴾ As though they had not remained in their graves except for the measure of an hour of the day; they will consider that period short because of the terror of what they encounter regarding the matter of resurrection and the Last Day. ﴿They will recognize one another.﴾ Some of them will know others. The word "ta'aruf" (mutual recognition) here is a recognition of rebuke, because each group will say to the other: "You led me astray," and similar things. ﴿Those who denied the meeting [with Allah] have certainly lost,﴾ the reward of Paradise, ﴿those who denied﴾ the resurrection.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 46:

﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them,﴾ he means: what they were afflicted with on the day of Badr. ﴿Or We take you (in death) before that,﴾ ﴿then to Us is their return,﴾ that is: then We will punish them in the Hereafter. ﴿Then Allah is Witness over what they do,﴾ of fighting you and denying you, so He will recompense them for it. The meaning of the verse is: if He does not take vengeance upon them in this world, He will take vengeance upon them in the next.

For every nation there is a messenger sent to them. ﴿And for every nation there is a messenger; when their messenger comes, judgment is passed between them with justice﴾, that is, the destruction of whoever denied him and the salvation of whoever followed him. ﴿And they will not be wronged﴾: the reward of the one who believed is not diminished, and the one who denied is recompensed for his denial.

﴿They say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ They said this when it was said to them: ﴿Whether We show you part of what We threaten them with﴾ (the verse), so they said: "When is this punishment you threaten us with, O Muhammad? ﴿If you are truthful﴾, you and your followers."
﴿Say: I possess no power to benefit or harm myself, except as God wills﴾. The verse is explained in two verses of Surat al-A'raf. When they hastened the punishment, it was said to the Prophet (ﷺ):

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 50:

﴿Say: Have you considered﴾, i.e., have you informed yourselves, ﴿if His punishment comes upon you by night﴾ while you sleep, ﴿or by day﴾ while you are awake, ﴿what is it that the criminals seek to hasten of it?﴾ That is, what is it that the criminals seek to hasten of the punishment? This is a question whose meaning is to magnify and to express the horror of the matter, i.e., how great is what they seek and hasten! Just as you say: "Have you considered what you are bringing upon yourself?!" When the Prophet (ﷺ) said this to them, they said: "We deny the punishment and we seek to hasten it; and when it occurs, we will believe in it." Then Allah, exalted is He, said:

﴿Then when it befalls you﴾ and descends upon you, ﴿you will believe in it﴾ after it has come down. But belief will not be accepted from you, and it will be said to you: ﴿Now?﴾ You will believe in it, ﴿while you used to be hasty about it﴾ in the world, mocking.

And they ask you (Prophet), ﴿Is it true?﴾ meaning: they ask you to inform them, "Is what you have told us of the punishment and the resurrection true?" Say, ﴿Yes, by my Lord, indeed it is true﴾ meaning: the punishment is descending upon you, ﴿and you cannot escape﴾ after death, meaning: you will be recompensed for your disbelief.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 54:

﴿And if every soul that had done wrong possessed whatever is on the earth, it would surely offer it as ransom﴾ — "done wrong" means "associated partners [with God]" — "it would surely offer it" — "it would give it up to ward off punishment from itself." ﴿And they will conceal the regret﴾ — "they will hide and keep secret" — "the regret" — meaning: the leaders among the lowly ones who misled them. ﴿And judgment will be passed between them﴾ — between the lowly ones and the leaders — ﴿with justice﴾ — "with fairness," so that each is recompensed for his deeds.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 55:

﴿Surely the promise of Allah is true﴾ — what He promised to His friends and His enemies. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ — meaning: the polytheists.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 57:

﴿O mankind﴾, meaning: the Quraysh. ﴿There has certainly come to you an admonition from your Lord﴾, namely the Qur'an, ﴿and a healing for what is in the breasts﴾, and a remedy for the disease of ignorance, ﴿and guidance﴾, and a clarification away from misguidance, ﴿and a mercy for the believers﴾, and a blessing from Allah, glorified is He, for the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Say, "By the bounty of Allah and by His mercy" — the bounty is Islam and the mercy is the Qur'an — "so let them rejoice in that; it is better" — meaning: what Allah has given them of Islam and the Qur'an is better than what others gather of the worldly life.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 59:

﴿Say﴾ to the disbelievers of Makkah: ﴿Have you considered what Allah has sent down﴾ — He created and brought it into being for you — ﴿of provision, and you made from it [some] unlawful and [some] lawful?﴾ Meaning: they made unlawful what was lawful for them, such as the baḥīrah and the like, and they made lawful what was unlawful, such as carrion and the like. ﴿Say, "Has Allah permitted you [to do so]?"﴾ in that prohibition and permission. ﴿Or﴾ rather, ﴿against Allah do you invent [falsehood]?﴾

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 60:

﴿And what will be the assumption of those who fabricate lies against Allah on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ That is: what will their assumption be on that Day concerning Allah, when they had fabricated lies against Him? ﴿Indeed, Allah is Full of bounty toward mankind﴾ — the people of Makkah — when He made them secure in a sanctuary, along with all the other blessings He bestowed upon them. ﴿But most of them do not give thanks.﴾ They do not affirm the Oneness of Allah, nor do they obey Him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 61:

﴿Wa-ma takūnu﴾ (And you are not), O Muhammad, ﴿fī sha'n﴾ (in any matter), of your affairs, ﴿wa-mā tatlū minhu﴾ (and you do not recite from Him), from God, ﴿min Qur'ān﴾ (any Qur'an) that He has sent down to you, ﴿wa-lā ta'malūna min 'amal﴾ (nor do you do any deed), addressed to him and his community, ﴿illā kunnā 'alaykum shuhūdan﴾ (except that We are witnesses over you), observing what you do, ﴿idh tufīḍūna﴾ (when you engage), you take up, ﴿fīhi﴾ (in it), ﴿wa-mā ya'zubu﴾ (and is not hidden), is concealed and remote, ﴿'an Rabbika min mithqāli dharratin﴾ (from your Lord, of even the weight of an atom), the weight of an atom, ﴿illā fī kitābin mubīn﴾ (but it is in a clear Book). He means: the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) in which God, glorified is He, recorded all created things.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 62:

﴿Indeed, the friends of Allah﴾ are those whom Allah, glorified is He, has taken charge of guiding.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 63:

﴿Those who believed﴾ affirmed the Prophet (ﷺ), ﴿and were mindful﴾ feared their standing before God, glorified is He.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 64:

﴿For them is good news in the life of this world﴾. At death, the angels come to them with good news from Allah. ﴿And in the Hereafter﴾, they are given good tidings of Allah's reward and His Garden. ﴿There is no altering of the words of Allah﴾: there is no breaking of His promises.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 65:

﴿And do not let their speech grieve you﴾ — i.e., their denial of you. ﴿Indeed, all might (al-'izzah) belongs to Allah﴾ — i.e., all strength belongs to Allah, and all power belongs to Allah. ﴿Entirely﴾ — and He is your Helper. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾ — He hears their speech. ﴿The All-Knowing﴾ — of what is in your hearts, so He will recompense them according to what their condition requires.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 66:

﴿Surely, to God belongs whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth.﴾ Meaning: He does with them and in them whatever He wills. ﴿And those who call upon other than God as partners do not really follow them.﴾ That is: they do not in truth follow partners, because they regard them as partners and intercessors for them, while they are not as they suppose. ﴿They follow nothing but conjecture.﴾ They follow nothing but their assumption that these will intercede for them. ﴿And they are merely guessing.﴾ They say what does not exist.

﴿He is the One who made the night for you that you may rest therein, and the day giving sight﴾: illuminating, so that you may be guided by it in your needs. ﴿Indeed, in that are signs for a people who hear﴾: hearing of i'tibar (reflection and drawing lessons).

"They say: 'Allah has taken a son.'" That is, their saying: the angels are the daughters of Allah. ﴿Glory be to Him!﴾ — exalting Him above what they have said. ﴿He is the Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani)﴾ — He does not need that He should have a wife or a son. ﴿You have no authority for this.﴾ That is, you have no proof for this.

Al-Wahidi's commentary (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 70:

And His saying: ﴿A brief enjoyment in the world﴾, meaning: for them there is an enjoyment in the world, which they enjoy for a few days.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 71:

And His saying: ﴿If my standing (among you) and my reminding you of the signs of Allah has been burdensome to you﴾ — that is, my staying and my sojourn among you has become great and difficult for you; ﴿and my reminding you of the signs of Allah﴾ — my admonition and my warning you of the punishment of Allah. ﴿Then in Allah have I put my trust﴾ — so do whatever you wish. This is His saying: ﴿So determine your affair and your partners﴾ — that is, resolve upon a firm plan on which you all agree. ﴿And your partners﴾ — along with your partners. It was also said: its meaning is: call upon your partners, meaning your gods. ﴿Then let not your affair be obscure to you⁠ — that is, let your affair be open and manifest, so that you may act in it as you wish, not like one who conceals a matter and hides it, so that he cannot do what he wants. ﴿Then carry out your plan against me﴾ — do what you intend, and proceed against me with what you dislike. ﴿And give me no respite﴾ — do not delay my affair. The meaning is: do not spare any effort in gathering and strength, for you will not be able to harm me, because I have a God who protects me. In this there is a strengthening of the heart of Muhammad (ﷺ), for his path with his people is like the path of the prophets before him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 72:

﴿Then if you turn away﴾, [i.e., turn away] from faith, ﴿then I have not asked you for any reward﴾, [i.e., any] wealth that you would give me. This is from the words of Noah (peace be upon him) to his people.

Its meaning: "So they would not believe in what those before them had denied" — that is, the nations of the prophets and messengers after Noah's people did not believe in what Noah's people had denied. In other words, these later ones did not believe in what their predecessors had denied, even though they knew that God, glory be to Him, had drowned those predecessors for their denial. Then He said: "Thus" — just as We set a seal upon their hearts — "We seal the hearts of the transgressors," those who go beyond the truth into falsehood.

And His saying: ﴿They said, "Have you come to us to turn us away from that which we found our fathers upon, and so that greatness in the land may belong to you two?"﴾ (to turn us away) from what we found our fathers upon. "Greatness" (al-kibriya'): the kingship and the might. "In the land": in the land of Egypt.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 81:

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah will nullify it﴾, i.e., will destroy it. ﴿Indeed, Allah does not set right the work of corruptors﴾, i.e., does not make it beneficial to them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 82:

﴿And Allah establishes the truth﴾ and makes it manifest by clear proofs, ﴿by His words﴾ by His promise.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 83:

﴿So none believed in Musa except a small group of his people,﴾ meaning: those from the Children of Israel who believed in him, and they were the offspring (dhurriyyah) of the sons of Ya'qub, ﴿out of fear of Fir'awn and their chiefs,﴾ meaning their leaders, ﴿that he would afflict them,﴾ meaning turn them away from their religion through a trial and a calamity he would inflict upon them. ﴿Indeed, Fir'awn was haughty﴾ meaning arrogant, ﴿on the earth,﴾ meaning in the land of Egypt, ﴿and indeed he was among the extravagant﴾ in that he was a servant who claimed lordship.

Translation of the passage:

And His words: ﴿Do not make us a trial for the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: Do not grant them victory over us, lest they see that they are better than us, so that they increase in rebellion and say: "Had they been upon the truth, we would not have been given power over them," and thus they would be led into trial.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 87:

﴿And We revealed to Musa and his brother﴾, etc. When Musa, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was sent to Fir'awn (Pharaoh), Fir'awn ordered the mosques of the Children of Israel to be destroyed, and all of them were ruined, and they were prevented from prayer. So they were commanded to take mosques in their houses and pray in them, out of fear of Fir'awn. That is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Settle your people in Egypt in houses﴾, i.e., take for them ﴿in Misr (Egypt) houses﴾ in their homes, ﴿and make your houses a qiblah﴾, i.e., pray in your houses so that you may be safe from fear.

"And His saying: ﴿Our Lord, that they may lead astray from Your way.﴾ That is: You made these possessions a cause of their going astray, because they were insolent and became arrogant against faith. ﴿Our Lord, obliterate their wealth﴾ — transform it and remove it from its form, so that their dirhams and dinars became stones, minted, both whole and halved; and likewise all their other wealth. ﴿And harden their hearts﴾ — seal them so that they do not soften and are not opened to faith. ﴿So they will not believe﴾ — an invocation against them. ﴿Until they see the painful punishment﴾ — meaning: drowning. So he was answered in that, and Pharaoh did not believe until drowning overtook him."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 89:

﴿He said: "Your supplication has been answered, so go straight"﴾ This was because Musa supplicated and Harun said "Amin". ﴿So go straight﴾ in the message and the call. ﴿And do not follow the way of those who do not know﴾ do not take the path of those who are ignorant of the reality of My promise, so that you hasten My decree.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 90:

And His saying: ﴿So Pharaoh pursued them, with his soldiers﴾. They sought to catch up with them, ﴿in insolence﴾, seeking to exalt themselves without right, ﴿and enmity﴾, through injustice. ﴿Until, when drowning overtook him﴾, he uttered what Allah related about him, when this did not benefit him, because he saw despair and witnessed it. Then it was said to him: ﴿Now? And you had disobeyed before﴾, meaning: Now you believe or repent? When Allah drowned him, some of the Children of Israel denied his drowning and said: "He is too great in stature to be drowned." So Allah, glorified is He, brought him out of the water until they saw him. This is His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 92:

﴿So today We will save you﴾ We will bring you out of the sea after drowning, ﴿in your body﴾ in your body that has no soul in it, ﴿so that you may be a sign for those after you﴾ a deterrent (nakāl) and a lesson. ﴿And indeed many of the people﴾ meaning the people of Makkah, ﴿are heedless of Our signs﴾ of what is intended for them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 93:

﴿And We certainly settled the Children of Israel in an excellent settlement﴾: We settled Qurayzah and al-Nadir in a place of truthfulness (manzil sidq), i.e., praiseworthy and chosen. He means: from the land of Yathrib, between Madinah and Syria. ﴿And We provided them with good things﴾: from the date palms and fruits, and We widened their provision. ﴿Yet they did not differ﴾ concerning the affirmation of the Prophet ﷺ and that he is a messenger sent, ﴿until knowledge came to them﴾: the reality of what they used to know, namely Muhammad (peace be upon him) by his description and attributes, and the Qur'an. That is because they used to inform about his time and his prophethood and believe in him. But when he came to them, they differed, and most of them disbelieved in him.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 94:

﴿If you are in doubt﴾ This, outwardly, is an address to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant by it is others among those who doubt the religion. And His saying: ﴿then ask those who have been reading the Book before you﴾ means: those among the People of the Book who believed, such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam and his companions, so that they may testify to the truthfulness of Muhammad and inform about his prophethood. The rest of the verse and the one that follows it are an address to the Prophet ﷺ, but what is meant by it is others.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 96:

﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified﴾ — that is, the word of punishment became binding upon them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 97:

﴿They will not believe.﴾ ﴿Even if every sign should come to them.﴾ This is because they used to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to bring them signs so that they would believe. Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ So faith will not benefit them at that time, just as it did not benefit Pharaoh.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 98:

﴿Why was there not a town that believed, so that its belief would benefit it?﴾ That is: there was no town that believed, so that its belief would benefit it at the descent of the punishment, ﴿except the people of Yunus. When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in this world﴾ at the descent of the punishment; ﴿and We let them enjoy for a time﴾. That is: the time of their terms. This is because, when they saw the signs that indicated the nearness of the punishment, they sincerely repented, returned the wrongs they had committed to their owners, and humbled themselves before Allah the Exalted, so the punishment was lifted from them.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 99:

﴿And if your Lord had willed, those on earth would have believed, all of them together﴾ (and so on, the verse continues). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was eager that all the people should believe, so Allah, glorified is He, informed him that none would believe except those for whom happiness had already been decreed by Allah, and that is His saying:

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 100:

﴿And it is not for any soul to believe except by the permission of Allah﴾. That is: except by what has preceded for it in the decree and destiny of Allah. ﴿And He places the abomination﴾, meaning the punishment, ﴿upon those who do not reason﴾ regarding the command and prohibition of Allah the Exalted, and what He calls them to.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 101:

Say, [O Muhammad], "Look at what is in the heavens and the earth": to the polytheists who ask you for signs. That is, look at what is greater than them of signs and lessons in the heavens and the earth which point to the oneness of Allah, the Exalted, so that they may know that all of that necessitates a Creator who is unlike things and to whom things are not alike. Then He explained that the signs do not benefit those whom Allah, the Exalted, knew in His knowledge would not believe, so He said: "But signs and warnings (nudhur, plural of nadhir) do not avail a people who do not believe." He says: warning is not beneficial to these people.

﴿Fa-hal yantazirun﴾ means: they ought not to await, after your denial, anything ﴿except the like of the days of those who passed away before them﴾, except like the encounters (waqa'i') of God, exalted is He, with those disbelievers of earlier times.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 103:

﴿Then We shall deliver Our messengers and those who believe.﴾ This is a report about what Allah, glorified is He, used to do with the earlier nations: delivering the messengers and those who affirmed them from the punishment with which He chastised those who disbelieved. ﴿Thus﴾ means: like this deliverance, ﴿We shall deliver the believers﴾ in Muhammad (ﷺ) from My punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 104:

﴿Say, "O mankind, if you are in doubt about my religion"﴾ He means the people of Makkah. ﴿Then I do not worship those you worship besides Allah﴾, i.e., despite your doubt concerning my religion, I do not worship anything other than Allah. ﴿But I worship Allah, who causes you to die﴾ takes your souls. In this there is a threat to them, because the death of the polytheists is the appointed time of their punishment.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 105:

And His saying: ﴿And [I was commanded], "Direct your face toward the religion, inclining to truth"﴾. Be upright by turning your full attention, with your face, to what you have been commanded.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 106:

﴿And do not invoke, other than Allah, that which neither benefits you nor harms you.﴾ That is: anything at all, because benefit and harm are only realized from Allah. So it is as if He had said: "And do not invoke anything other than Allah."

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 107:

﴿And if Allah touches you with harm﴾ — with sickness and poverty — ﴿there is no remover of it except Him﴾ — no one who removes it — ﴿And if He intends for you good﴾ — He brings good to you — ﴿there is no repeller of His bounty﴾ — no one who withholds what He has bestowed upon you of ease and blessing — ﴿He causes it to reach whom He wills of His servants﴾ — with each of what has been mentioned.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 108:

﴿Say, "O mankind"﴾ meaning: the people of Makkah. ﴿The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord﴾ the Qur'an, and in it is clarification and healing. ﴿So whoever is guided﴾ from misguidance, ﴿then he is guided only for [the benefit of] himself﴾ meaning: whoever believes in Muhammad (peace be upon him), he is only taking precaution for himself. ﴿And whoever goes astray﴾ by denying him, ﴿then he errs only against himself﴾ the consequence of his misguidance falls only upon himself. ﴿And I am not over you a guardian﴾ a protector from destruction, so that you would not be destroyed.

Commentary of al-Wahidi (al-Wajiz) on surah 10, verse 109:

﴿And follow what is revealed to you, and be patient until Allah judges﴾ It was abrogated (nusikhat) by the verse of the sword, because Allah, glorified is He, has decreed the killing of the polytheists and the jizya (poll-tax) upon the People of the Book.
